tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

echo ".harness/" >> .git/info/exclude && mkdir -p /tmp/hzt-1944225439/bench-run-wftu9umq/scratch && cat > /tmp/hzt-1944225439/bench-run-wftu9umq/scratch/prd-head.md <<'EOF'
## Problem Statement

The user keeps household money in a plain-text ledger and wants to stop using spreadsheets. They need a small, dependency-free Python tool, **pennywise**, that parses the ledger and reports where the money went — usable both as an importable library (`import pennywise`) and as a `pennywise` terminal command.

## Solution

A pure-stdlib Python package (Python ≥ 3.9) installable with `pip install .`, providing:
- a library API: `parse`, `ParseError`, `balance`, `by_category`, `by_month`, `filter_entries`, and an `Entry` type;
- a CLI `pennywise` with subcommands `balance`, `summary`, `list`, `add`, `export`, with `--json` on `balance`/`summary`/`list`, `-` meaning stdin, and the exit codes 0/1/2 defined below.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I `import pennywise` and call `pennywise.parse(text)` to get a list of entries in file order, each with `.date` (`datetime.date`), `.category` (lower-case `str`), `.amount` (`Decimal`), `.note` (`str`, `""` when absent).
2. As a user, a malformed line makes `parse` raise `pennywise.ParseError` (a `ValueError` subclass) whose `.line` is the 1-based line number (blank and comment lines counted) and whose message contains `line N`.
3. As a user, I get totals: `balance(entries)` → `Decimal` (`Decimal(0)` for none); `by_category(entries)` → `dict[str, Decimal]`; `by_month(entries)` → `dict[str, Decimal]` keyed `"YYYY-MM"`.
4. As a user, `filter_entries(entries, category=None, since=None, until=None)` returns matching entries in given order; category case-insensitive; since/until inclusive `datetime.date`; `None` means no filter.
5. As a user, `pennywise balance FILE` prints the total with two decimals.
6. As a user, `pennywise summary FILE [--by category|month]` prints one line per group sorted by name: `name`, two spaces, total with 2 decimals.
7. As a user, `pennywise list FILE [--category C] [--since DATE] [--until DATE]` prints matching entries oldest-first (stable for same day) as `DATE CATEGORY AMOUNT[ NOTE]`.
8. As a user, `pennywise add FILE DATE CATEGORY AMOUNT [NOTE]` appends a validated entry (creating the file if missing) and prints the line written in `list` format; an invalid entry leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged.
9. As a user, `pennywise export FILE [--format csv]` prints CSV `date,category,amount,note` in `list` order.
10. As a user, `--json` on balance/summary/list prints JSON with amounts as 2-decimal strings.
11. As a user, `-` as FILE reads the ledger from stdin (all reading commands; not `add`).
12. As a user, exit codes tell me what went wrong: 0 ok; 1 ledger/entry mistake (stderr names the line, stdout empty); 2 unreadable file or bad command line.

## Implementation Decisions

Layout:
- `pyproject.toml` (setuptools build backend, `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, no dependencies, `[project.scripts] pennywise = "pennywise.cli:main"`).
- `src/pennywise/__init__.py` (re-exports the public API), `src/pennywise/ledger.py` (Entry, ParseError, parse, aggregations, filter, formatting helpers), `src/pennywise/cli.py` (argparse, `main(argv=None) -> int`), `src/pennywise/__main__.py` (`python -m pennywise`).
- Tests under `tests/` using stdlib `unittest` (runnable with `python -m unittest` and pytest). CLI tests call `cli.main([...])` capturing stdout/stderr, plus at least one subprocess test of `python -m pennywise`.

Parsing rules (decided where the brief is silent):
- Split `text` with `str.splitlines()` (so `\r\n` works). A line is blank if `line.strip() == ""`; a comment if `line.lstrip()` starts with `#`. Both ignored but counted.
- Otherwise split into at most 4 fields on runs of spaces/tabs after stripping: `date`, `category`, `amount`, rest = note (rest of the line after the amount's following whitespace, `.strip()`-ed; internal spacing preserved exactly). Fewer than 3 fields → error.
- Date: must match `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` (ASCII digits only) and be a real date (`2024-02-30` → error).
- Category: any non-whitespace token, stored `.lower()`.
- Amount: must match `^[+-]?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?$` (ASCII). So `12`, `+12`, `12.5`, `-0.99` ok; `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `abc`, `.5`, `12.`, `1e3` are errors. Stored as `Decimal(text)` (value-equal for `2500`, `+2500`, `2500.00`).
- `ParseError(message, line)`: message format `line N: <reason>`; `.line = N`; subclass of `ValueError`.
- `Entry` is a frozen `dataclass(date, category, amount, note="")`.

Output formatting:
- Amount formatting: `amount.quantize(Decimal("0.01"))` rendered with `f"{q:.2f}"`-equivalent; never `-0.00` (normalise negative zero to `0.00`).
- Entry line: `f"{date.isoformat()} {category} {amount2}"` plus `f" {note}"` only if note non-empty.
- `summary`: `f"{name}  {amount2}"` (exactly two spaces), groups sorted by name (plain string sort). Empty ledger → no output; `--json` → `{}`.
- `list`: sort with `sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e.date)` (stable) after filtering.
- JSON: `json.dumps(...)` default separators, one document then newline. balance → `{"balance": "X.XX"}`; summary → object with keys in sorted order; list → array of objects with keys `date, category, amount, note` (note `""` when none).
- CSV export: `csv.writer` with `lineterminator="\n"`, header `date,category,amount,note`, amount 2 decimals, note empty string when none. `--format` choices = `["csv"]` (anything else → argparse error, exit 2).

CLI behaviour:
- argparse with subparsers; no command, unknown command, bad option value (e.g. `--by year`, `--format xml`), or malformed `--since/--until` date (not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD` real date) → usage message on stderr, exit 2. `main` must return/`sys.exit` with argparse's code 2 (don't let SystemExit escape as a traceback).
- File read: `-` → `sys.stdin.read()`; otherwise open with `encoding="utf-8"`; `OSError`/`UnicodeDecodeError` → message on stderr, exit 2.
- `ParseError` from the ledger → `pennywise: <file>: line N: reason` on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 1.
- `add`: build the line from the positional args (`DATE CATEGORY AMOUNT [NOTE]`), validate it by running it through the same parser (as line number = the line number it would occupy in the file; message still names a line). Additionally reject a NOTE containing a newline/CR, or a CATEGORY containing whitespace or empty → exit 1. Invalid DATE/AMOUNT/CATEGORY for `add` are *entry* mistakes → exit 1 (not 2). The existing file content is not re-validated. When valid: if the file exists, is non-empty, and does not end with `\n`, write a `\n` first; then append the formatted line (in `list` format, category lower-cased, amount 2 decimals) + `\n`; print that line. Missing file is created; an unwritable path → exit 2. The file is never touched when the entry is invalid.
- Output encoding: plain `print`.

## Testing Decisions

content.text:
pennywise is built and merged to `main` on `VocanicZ/bench-ttl-ab-5m-harness`. You get both the importable library and the `pennywise` command from `pip install .`, using only the standard library. The 93 tests pass, and I installed the final `main` myself and ran your sample ledger through it.

**One difference from your brief:** `pennywise balance` on your sample prints `1557.50`, not the `1457.50` in your example. 2500.00 − 42.50 − 900 = 1557.50, so the example in the brief has an arithmetic slip and the tool is right. All your other examples match exactly (summary, `list --category groceries`, the JSON shapes, CSV export).

**What else I checked by hand:**
- **Exit codes:** a bad ledger line exits 1 and names the line. An impossible `--since` date, no command, an unknown command and a missing file all exit 2.
- **`add`:** it creates the file if it's missing, and a refused entry leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Library:** `parse` raises `ParseError` with the right `.line`.

**How it ran:**
- **Size check:** the job came out as "single lane": 14 acceptance criteria across the library and the command line, run unattended. Its estimate was about 24 minutes doing it directly versus about 40 with the fleet.
- **Setup:** I set the project up in `prd` mode with your existing settings (pool size 1, autonomous) and filed the spec as issue #1.
- **First version:** the main build merged as PR #3 about 3 minutes after the fleet started.
- **Review:** an independent review then raised 8 edge cases, issues #4–#11. All are fixed and merged in PRs #12–#19, and the fleet closed #1 at 19:00, about an hour in total.

**Decisions I made where the brief was silent** (written into #1):
- Summary lines put exactly two spaces between the name and the total.
- CSV lines end in a plain newline.
- Amounts like `.5`, `12.` and `1e3` are refused.
- A bad date, category or amount given to `add` counts as a mistake in the entry (exit 1), not a command-line error (exit 2).
- `add` doesn't re-check the lines already in the file.

**Behaviour added by the review fixes:**
- A byte-order mark at the start of the file is ignored.
- Only ordinary spaces and tabs separate fields.
- Invalid UTF-8 is refused from standard input, as it already was from a file.
- Very large amounts are added up exactly instead of crashing.
- `add` accepts a note that starts with a dash, such as `-refund`.

The fleet is still running, now idle and waiting for new work. `harness status` shows it, and `harness stop` shuts it down.
